Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

cd "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-bodhishthomas-code-care-fe/cf4cdbbe-a1e2-43de-aa1d-d77f31bdfcef/scratchpad" && jq -s '
  (.[1] | map({key: (.number|tostring), value: .}) | from_entries) as $ts
  | .[0] | map(
      . as $p
      | ($ts[($p.number|tostring)]) as $t
      | ([.labels[].name]) as $L
      | ([.reviews[] | select(.s=="APPROVED" and (.by|test("github-actions|copilot|coderabbit|\\[bot\\]")|not)) | .by]) as $app
      | ([$t.latestOpinionatedReviews.nodes[] | select(.state=="CHANGES_REQUESTED")]) as $cha
      | ($cha | map(.submittedAt) | max) as $lastCha
      | ($t.commits.nodes[0].commit.committedDate) as $lc
      | (if (.author.login=="app/github-actions") then "1_BOT_PLAYWRIGHT"
         elif (.author.login|test("^app/(renovate|dependabot)")) then "2_BOT_DEPS"
         elif (.isDraft or ($L|index("Work in Progress")) or ($L|index("do not merge")) or ($L|index("backlog")) or (.title|test("^Test:"))) then "9_WIP_PARKED"
         elif (($cha|length)>0 and $lc > $lastCha) then "6_CHA_AWAIT_REREVIEW"
         elif (($cha|length)>0) then "7_CHA_AWAIT_AUTHOR"
         elif (($app|length)>0 and .mergeable=="MERGEABLE" and .ci=="SUCCESS") then "3_READY"
         elif (($app|length)>0 and .mergeable=="CONFLICTING") then "5_APPROVED_CONFLICT"
         elif (($app|length)>0) then "4_APPROVED_CI_RED"
         else "8_NEEDS_FIRST_REVIEW" end) as $bucket
      | {number, title, author: .author.login, bucket: $bucket, approvals: $app, cha: ($cha|map(.author.login)), mergeable, ci, isDraft, fork: .isCrossRepository, labels: $L, created: .createdAt[0:10], updated: .updatedAt[0:10], lastCommit: ($lc[0:10]), size: "+\(.additions)/-\(.deletions)", files: .changedFiles, base: .baseRefName, closes}
    )' merged.json prs_reviews_ts.json > classified.json
echo "=== bucket counts"; jq -r 'group_by(.bucket) | map("\(.[0].bucket)\t\(length)") | .[]' classified.json; jq -r '"TOTAL\t\(length)"' classified.json
echo; echo "=== non-bot buckets"
jq -r 'map(select(.bucket|test("^[3-9]"))) | sort_by(.bucket, -(.number)) | .[] | [.bucket, .number, .author, (if .fork then "fork" else "" end), (.approvals|length|tostring)+"app", (.cha|join("+")), .mergeable[0:4], .ci[0:4], .created, .lastCommit, .size, .title[0:70]] | @tsv' classified.json

content.text:
I put all 118 open PRs into eight buckets by what each needs next; the counts are computed from the GitHub data and sum to 118.

| Bucket | Count |
|---|---|
| A. Ready to merge | 12 |
| A′. QA-approved, needs a code reviewer | 2 |
| B. Approved but blocked (conflict or real CI failure) | 7 |
| C. Changes requested, author has pushed, reviewer owes a re-review | 18 |
| D. Changes requested, waiting on the author | 10 |
| E. Needs a first review | 9 |
| F. WIP, draft or parked | 15 |
| G. `daily-playwright` bot | 28 |
| H. Dependency bots (Renovate and Dependabot) | 17 |

Red CI is not a reliable signal in this repo right now.
- Playwright on `develop` failed its last two pushes and is roughly 50/50 over the last 40 runs.
- 12 of the 64 red PRs are red only because the AI reviewer workflows failed or were cancelled.
- 10 more are red only for the JIRA title or label checks.

I counted those as not really failing. "Author has pushed" in bucket C means the last commit is newer than the last changes-requested review, so a plain merge from `develop` also counts.

(.[1] | map({key:(.number|tostring), value:.}) | from_entries) as $m
| (.[2] | map({key:(.number|tostring), value:.}) | from_entries) as $ts
| (.[3] | map({key:(.number|tostring), value:.kind}) | from_entries) as $ck
| ["Care Fe Code Reviewers","Care Frontend Maintainers","Care QA","Core Team",""] as $teams
| [ .[0][]
    | select(.number != 16610 and .number != 16736)
    | (.number|tostring) as $k

    | (if .number==16455 then "CONFLICTING" else .mergeable end) as $mg
    | ([ $ts[$k].latestOpinionatedReviews.nodes[] | select(.state=="CHANGES_REQUESTED") | {by:.author.login, at:.submittedAt, stale:(.submittedAt < $lc)} ]) as $chas
    | (.bucket) as $b0
    | (if .number==16762 then "6_CHA_AWAIT_REREVIEW" else $b0 end) as $b1
    | ($ck[$k] // (if .ci=="SUCCESS" then "GREEN" else .ci end)) as $cik
    | (if $b1=="3_READY" and (.approvals==["nihal467"]) then "A2_QA_ONLY"
       elif $b1=="3_READY" then "A_READY"
       elif $b1=="4_APPROVED_CI_RED" and $cik=="REVIEWER_BOT_ONLY" and (.approvals==["nihal467"]) then "A2_QA_ONLY"
       elif $b1=="4_APPROVED_CI_RED" and $cik=="REVIEWER_BOT_ONLY" then "A_READY"
       elif ($b1=="4_APPROVED_CI_RED" or $b1=="5_APPROVED_CONFLICT") then "B_BLOCKED"
       elif $b1=="6_CHA_AWAIT_REREVIEW" then "C_REREVIEW"
       elif $b1=="7_CHA_AWAIT_AUTHOR" then "D_AUTHOR"
       elif $b1=="8_NEEDS_FIRST_REVIEW" then "E_FIRST"
       elif $b1=="9_WIP_PARKED" then "F_WIP"
       else $b1 end) as $st
    | . + {status:$st, lastCommit:($lc[0:10]), mergeable:$mg, cikind:$cik, chas:$chas,
           requested: ([$m[$k].requested[] | select(. as $r | $teams | index($r) | not)]),
           assignees: ([$m[$k].assignees[].login | select(.!="Copilot" and .!="Claude")]) }
  ] as $prs
| {
    counts: ($prs | group_by(.status) | map({(.[0].status): length}) | add),
    total: ($prs|length),
    authored: ($prs | map(select(.author|test("^app/")|not)) | group_by(.author) | map({user:.[0].author, n:length, prs: (sort_by(.status, -(.number)) | map({number,status,title:(.title|gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$";"")|.[0:80]),approvals:(.approvals|length),mergeable:.mergeable[0:4],cikind,lastCommit,size,fork,owedBy:([.chas[]|select(.stale)|.by]), chaBy:([.chas[]|.by])}))}) | sort_by(-.n)),
    agentAssigned: ($prs | map(select(.author|test("^app/(copilot|anthropic)"))) | map({number,status,assignees,title:.title[0:70],mergeable:.mergeable[0:4],cikind})),
    rereviewOwed: ([ $prs[] | select(.status!="F_WIP" and (.author|test("^app/github-actions")|not)) | . as $p | .chas[] | select(.stale) | {reviewer:.by, number:$p.number, author:$p.author, since:.at[0:10], pushed:$p.lastCommit, status:$p.status, mergeable:$p.mergeable[0:4]} ] | group_by(.reviewer) | map({reviewer:.[0].reviewer, n:length, items:.}) | sort_by(-.n)),
    reviewRequested: ([ $prs[] | select(.status!="F_WIP") | . as $p | .requested[] | . as $r | select(($p.chas | map(select(.stale) | .by) | index($r)) | not) | {reviewer:$r, number:$p.number, author:$p.author, status:$p.status} ] | group_by(.reviewer) | map({reviewer:.[0].reviewer, n:length, items: (map("#\(.number)(\(.author);\(.status[0:1]))"))}) | sort_by(-.n))
  }
EOF

=== #15853
Fix React Query cache persistence across logout and invalidate patient cache after update 
**Describe the bug**
On logout, the React Query cache is not fully cleared. Only the `["currentUser"]` query is reset, while all other cached queries (e.g., `["patient", id]`, `["diagnosticReport", id]`, `["facility", id]`) remain in memory for the lifetime of the browser tab.
On shared workstations, this can result in previously fetched patient data being rendered briefly in a new user session before the background refetch completes.
This creates a cross-session data boundary issue.

name: project-pr-issue-triage
description: How Bodhish likes care_fe PR/issue triage done (buckets by next action, per-user view, issue clusters) + gh/GitHub gotchas specific to this repo
metadata:
  type: project
---

Bodhish asked (2026-09-19/20) to classify all open PRs, regroup them per user, and cluster all open issues for ohcnetwork/care_fe. He acted on the output immediately (merged two "ready" PRs), so this is likely a recurring ask.

**Scheme that worked**
- PRs by *next action*: ready / QA-approved-only / approved-but-blocked / changes-requested→re-review owed / changes-requested→author's move / needs first review / WIP-parked / daily-playwright bot / dependency bots.
- Per-user view = authored PRs by status **plus re-reviews each reviewer owes** (reviewer's CHANGES_REQUESTED older than author's last push; exclude draft/WIP and PRs where a newer CHA from someone else is unanswered).
- Issues clustered by content (labels are process-only: stale / needs-triage / question; no area labels exist). Split automation noise from real issues first.

**Repo-specific gotchas**
- `gh pr list --json` with heavy fields (statusCheckRollup, reviews) returns HTTP 502 at this repo's size — split into light calls + paginated GraphQL (page size 30). `gh api graphql --paginate` requires the cursor variable to be named `$endCursor`, otherwise it loops on page one forever.
- `reviewDecision` is mostly empty here (reviews not required by branch protection) — derive state from `latestOpinionatedReviews`. Exclude `github-actions` approvals (that's the AI "CARE PR Reviewer"), and treat a lone `nihal467` approval as QA pass only, not code review.
- CI rollup red is unreliable: AI reviewer workflows (CARE PR Reviewer / Grumpy) fail or get cancelled and count as red; JIRA-title validation fails on untitled PRs; Playwright on `develop` was ~50% pass. Check failing workflow names via `gh pr checks <n> --json name,state,workflow` before calling a PR blocked.
- Mergeability can change without `updatedAt` moving — re-query `mergeable` after merges into develop.

**Snapshot 2026-09-20:** 116 open PRs (45 bot: 28 daily-playwright covering only 13 targets, 17 deps with renovate+dependabot duplicates); 179 open issues (46 automation: 37 agentic-workflow failure reports, 8 daily coverage trackers, 1 renovate dashboard). Related: [[project-improve-plans-workflow]] (the 2026-07-08 audit issues #16507–#16524 are still open, mostly unassigned).

I clustered all 179 open issues by reading their titles and, where a title was ambiguous, the body. The repo has no area labels; the existing ones are process labels like `stale`, `needs-triage` and `question`. Every issue sits in exactly one cluster. 46 of the 179 are automation-generated; the other 133 were filed by people, plus 3 by CodeRabbit.

| Cluster | Issues | Unassigned | With an open PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Automation-generated** | **46** | | |
| Agentic-workflow failure reports | 37 | 31 | 3 |
| Daily Playwright coverage trackers | 8 | 8 | – |
| Renovate dependency dashboard | 1 | – | – |
| **Product areas** | **78** | | |
| Pharmacy, medications and inventory | 12 | 2 | 1 |
| Encounter and clinical charting | 12 | 5 | 1 |
| Facility admin and settings | 12 | 7 | 1 |
| Scheduling, appointments and queue | 11 | 5 | 1 |
| Questionnaires and valuesets | 8 | 5 | – |

| UI polish, accessibility and i18n | 10 | 2 | 3 |
| Tech debt and code quality | 9 | 3 | 2 |
| Permissions and security | 8 | 3 | 1 |
| Performance and architecture | 4 | 4 | 1 |
| Reliability (request, auth, upload) | 3 | 2 | – |
| Plugins and platform | 2 | 0 | – |
| Docs and build | 2 | 2 | 1 |

## Product areas

**Pharmacy, medications and inventory (12)**
- **P1:** [#15499](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/15499), delivery order totals.
- **Dispense:**
  - [#15413](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/15413): cancelling an invoice should offer to cancel the dispense.
  - [#15472](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/15472): the dispense atom is null when the URL is opened directly.
  - [#15547](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/15547): print prescriptions from the dispense view (blocked).
  - [#15354](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/15354): the QR scan shows a placeholder name.
- **Medication requests and administration:**
  - [#16356](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/16356): layout breaks when frequency is empty.
  - [#16095](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/16095): category on medication requests.
  - [#15938](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/15938): show note and method in the drug chart.
  - [#11946](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/11946): the dosage popover closes on Android keyboard focus.
- **Products:**
  - [#16127](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/16127) and [#14521](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/14521) are near-duplicate Product Knowledge mobile layout issues. [PR #16140](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/pull/16140) covers the second.
  - [#13865](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/issues/13865): product definition not deleted (backend).

**Encounter and clinical charting (12)**
